clue.text: Order more TV ie. extra for working class

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch more television, a bonus for the working class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command to watch more TV, but it signals that the letters of MORE TV IE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours worked beyond the normal shift earn extra pay, a familiar bonus for wage earners.

clue.text: Player is appearing in special make of boot

indicators.note: appearing in places the little word is inside the rearranged footwear
a special make of the boot is a different build, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer turns out in a special brand of boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a footballer in his boots, but it is a musician. 'special make of' signals the rearrangement and 'appearing in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind musician playing the double-reed instrument is a player in an orchestra.

clue.text: No such trees in the nursery?

definitions.text: No such trees in the nursery?

parts.words: No such trees in the nursery
parts.note: a nursery holds young children and young saplings, so senior people are not found there, though the word also names a shrub

explanation.surface: A question about which trees a plant nursery lacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery' suggests a garden centre, but it is a children's room; seniors are not there, though they share a name with a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior members of a community are older people, and the word also names an elderberry shrub; neither fits a room for infants.

clue.text: Decay in excellent pie upset restaurant

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the whole run upside down, so it reads backwards
in places the word for decay inside the pair of words for excellent and pie

explanation.surface: Rot in a fine pie upsets an eating place.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is written AI. 'in' signals the insertion, and 'upset', in a down clue, turns the whole assembled run upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian eating house serving simple food is a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Vessel Shylock wanted to catch Antonio on

definitions.text: Shylock wanted to catch Antonio on

explanation.surface: Shylock longed to seize Antonio aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice, Shylock says of Antonio 'If I can catch him once upon the hip'; Antonio is the merchant, so the merchant's hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A trading boat carries goods for commerce, and split differently the phrase names the body part of Shakespeare's Venetian trader.

clue.text: More work — that's too good to be true

definitions.text: that's too good to be true

explanation.surface: Someone groans at more work, saying it all seems too good to be true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, the Tudor statesman; the capital is hidden at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's best-known book describes an ideal island state, and the title became the word for any impossibly perfect place.

clue.text: Spells of duty in French town

explanation.surface: Periods of service in a town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Stints of service, as in a soldier's posting, are called by this word, and it is also a city on the Loire.

clue.text: Order to repair city

indicators.note: an order given to repair something is read as putting these letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An instruction is issued to restore a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' seems to be a command, but it signals rearranging the letters of TO REPAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: South Africa's administrative capital is a city in Gauteng.

clue.text: Jack's article about fashionable drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sailor's and article pair goes round the word for fashionable

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, AB, and the 's gives ABS

explanation.surface: A sailor's piece about a trendy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: AB (able seaman) is a common crossword sailor, like jack tar. 'about' signals that the sailor's article goes round the word for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A green, wormwood-flavoured spirit is a strong drink.

clue.text: One of 2? The deuce he is!

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at someone's identity.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' points to 2-down, ELDERS: an old Harry is an elder. 'The deuce' is an old euphemism for the Devil, whose nickname this is.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly man named Harry is one of the elders, and the phrase is also a folk nickname for Satan, like 'the deuce'.

clue.text: Compulsion to clothe' upstart

annotationWithheld.why: Compulsion to clothe' upstart (6): DURESS as DRESS round U needs 'clothe' to give DRESS and also signal the container; no separate indicator word is left.

clue.text: How dramatic success is achieved finally

explanation.surface: Explaining how theatrical success comes about in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A hit play enjoys a long run in the theatre; the phrase also means eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage hit plays for many months, and the idiom also means eventually, after everything has played out.

clue.text: Fish for one of a couple of fussy eaters

definitions.text: one of a couple of fussy eaters

explanation.surface: A fish is served for one of two picky diners.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Jack Sprat could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean: a pair of fussy eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like food fish shares its name with Jack of the rhyme, one half of a famously choosy couple.

clue.text: Win so easily at half past six?

explanation.surface: A question about winning comfortably at a particular time of day.
explanation.walkthrough: At half past six both clock hands point straight down.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey who wins without urging lets his grip relax, the idiom for an effortless victory; on a clock face at 6:30 both pointers aim at the bottom.

clue.text: What makes the Cabinet shine at languages?

parts.note: French is a language of France
Polish is a language of Poland

explanation.surface: A question about what makes the government Cabinet sparkle in foreign tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' with its capital suggests ministers, but it is a piece of furniture given a glossy finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellac finish rubbed onto wooden furniture gives it a high gloss, so it makes a cabinet gleam.

clue.text: Notes arrangement to get first goal

explanation.surface: Rearranging notes to get the first goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the definition: musical notes set out with a stave per part.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical layout giving each part its own staff is so called, and to make the opening goal of a match is to start the tally.

clue.text: Not Christian saint — I can go wrong

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A non-believer protests that a saint can go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ST and I CAN GO together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that God's existence cannot be known is no believer, so not a Christian.

clue.text: Deliver wine — there's no duty, here

parts.note: to deliver someone is to free them

explanation.surface: Deliver wine to a place where no tax is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour zone where imports are exempt from customs charges is a duty-free place.

clue.text: European pirate provides mixture of metals

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate of Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A European buccaneer supplies an alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickel silver is an alloy of copper, zinc and nickel containing no actual silver, a blend of metals.

clue.text: Fair split by state lawyer

indicators.note: split by means cut open with something put in, so the word for fair is broken by the state

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A fair is divided by a state lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like a noun, a funfair, but it is the adjective. 'split by' signals the insertion of the US state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in law, especially a judge or legal scholar, is such a person.

clue.text: He arranges adjustment of tie-rod

indicators.note: an adjustment of a part changes its setting, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic arranges to adjust a car's tie-rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment of' rearranges the letters of TIE-ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prepares and orders material for publication arranges it.

clue.text: Choice about time for military action

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for choice is placed round the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A choice regarding when to launch a military strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choice' heads the clue as if it were the definition, but the definition is 'military action' at the end; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned military campaign or manoeuvre is called by this name.

clue.text: Stone an aged, aged man' was a-sitting on

definitions.text: an aged, aged man' was a-sitting on

explanation.surface: A quotation about a stone an old man sat on.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's White Knight's song in Through the Looking-Glass, 'an aged aged man, a-sitting on a gate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded chalcedony is a gemstone, and split as two words it names the gate where Carroll's old man sat.

clue.text: Dive deep in well

explanation.surface: Someone is plunging deep into a well.
explanation.walkthrough: A whale sounds when it dives steeply; 'well' is the adjective, as in safe and well.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales are said to sound when they plunge downwards, and healthy or undamaged things are described with this word.

clue.text: Hard worker involved in long-term investment

explanation.surface: A diligent employee is tied up in a long-term financial investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' is the old sense of siege: the ten-year siege of Troy involved the people of Troy. One works like a ___ when working hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'work like a Trojan' makes one a hard worker, and the besieged citizens of Troy were caught up in a ten-year siege.

clue.text: Crime prevention no match for him?

definitions.text: Crime prevention no match for him?

parts.words: Crime prevention no match for him
parts.note: read as keeping matches away from a criminal, denying him the means to start a fire

explanation.surface: A villain so skilled that crime prevention can't compete with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no match for him' seems to mean outclassed, but read literally it means do not give him a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser needs a match, so keeping one from him prevents his offence.

clue.text: One who splits deck in vessel

explanation.surface: Someone splits the deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' is a deck of cards, not a ship's deck, though the second sense is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A card player who divides the pack before dealing cuts it, and a small fast boat goes by the same name.

clue.text: He's responsible for the child, of necessity

definitions.text: He's responsible for the child, of necessity

parts.words: He's responsible for the child, of necessity
parts.note: plays on the proverb that necessity is the mother of invention, so the child is a new device and its creator is responsible

explanation.surface: A father is necessarily responsible for his child.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Necessity is the mother of invention' makes any new device the child of necessity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who devises a new contraption brings into being the offspring of necessity in the proverb.
